Bug Title: Market switch revalidates only the settings key so every catalog cache keeps serving the previous market
Bug Description: resolveMarketForCountry in src/helpers/market.ts:11-28 sets the market cookie at :19 - calls switchMarket at :20 - then awaits mutate('/settings') at :21 and nothing else. CLAUDE.md 7.4 requires a market switch to invalidate all catalog caches (products - categories - brands - stores - home layout - search). Those SWR keys are never mutated so they keep serving the previous market payload while /settings returns the NEW market currency symbol and format through SettingsContext at src/contexts/SettingsContext.tsx:118-128. The result is the old market prices rendered with the new market currency symbol.
Preconditions: Two markets configured with different currencies and different catalog or pricing. User has browsed a category or the home page so those SWR keys are populated.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Browse the home page and a category listing in market A so SWR caches them. 2. Change the delivery location to a country that maps to market B which calls resolveMarketForCountry. 3. Without a hard reload return to the home page or the category listing.
Expected Result: All catalog caches are invalidated on market switch so products - categories - brands - stores - home layout and search refetch under the new X-Market header.
Actual Result: Only the settings key revalidates. Catalog lists still show market A products and market A price amounts now labelled with market B currency symbol.
Impact: Customer sees another market inventory and mispriced products. Any add-to-cart from that stale list carries a product that may not be sellable in the active market.
Suggested Fix: In resolveMarketForCountry invalidate every catalog SWR key after switchMarket - either by calling mutate with a key predicate that matches the catalog endpoints or by bumping a market scoped key prefix so all catalog keys change on switch.

Bug Title: withAuth silently does nothing on checkout and payment because neither route is listed in PROTECTED_ROUTES
Bug Description: isProtectedRoute at src/guards/authGuard.ts:15-23 matches with strict equality path === route against PROTECTED_ROUTES at :5-13. That list holds /cart - /my-account - /my-account/orders - /my-account/addresses - /my-account/wallet - /my-account/transactions - /my-account/refer-and-earn. CheckoutPage is wrapped by withAuth at src/pages/cart/checkout/index.tsx:79 and its router.pathname is /cart/checkout which is not in the list. PaymentPage is wrapped at src/pages/payment/[slug].tsx:62 and its router.pathname is /payment/[slug] which is not in the list either. withAuth at src/guards/withAuth.tsx:16-25 therefore never enters its redirect branch. Neither page performs any token check in getServerSideProps - unlike the my-account pages which check getAccessTokenFromContext inline (for example src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:345-356) - so both routes are completely unguarded.
Preconditions: User is logged out. The site is running with NEXT_PUBLIC_SSR set to true.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log out or open a clean private window. 2. Navigate directly to /cart/checkout/ and then to /payment/anything.
Expected Result: The visitor is redirected away and prompted to sign in - the same behaviour the my-account routes already implement server side.
Actual Result: Both pages render for an anonymous visitor. The guard never fires because the pathname never matches the list.
Impact: Two authenticated-only routes ship with an auth control that looks present in code review but is inert. Checkout and payment shells render for anonymous users and the underlying API 401 then triggers a global logout which is a confusing dead end.
Suggested Fix: Add /cart/checkout and /payment/[slug] to PROTECTED_ROUTES and switch isProtectedRoute to a prefix match so nested and dynamic routes are covered. Better still add a server side token check to both pages in getServerSideProps so the guard does not depend on client state.

Bug Title: Bearer token and the full user record are stored in JavaScript readable cookies with no CSP in place
Bug Description: setCookie in src/lib/cookies.ts:12-51 writes cookies through document.cookie so the httpOnly flag can never be set. helpers/auth.ts stores both the bearer token and the entire user object with it at :104-105 (google) - :209-210 (apple) - :598-599 (password) and :756-757 (phone OTP). The interceptor reads the token back client side at src/routes/interceptor.ts:29. next.config.ts sets HSTS - X-Frame-Options - nosniff - Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy but sets NO Content-Security-Policy - and images.dangerouslyAllowSVG is true with remotePatterns hostname ** which widens the script injection surface. Any XSS therefore reads document.cookie and lifts a valid Sanctum bearer token plus the user name - email and mobile.
Preconditions: An XSS sink anywhere in the storefront. Note the storefront renders API supplied HTML in places which is reviewed separately in later sessions.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Trigger any script execution in the page origin. 2. Read document.cookie. 3. Replay the access_token value as an Authorization Bearer header against the panel API.
Expected Result: The session token is not reachable from page JavaScript - an httpOnly cookie still lets getAccessTokenFromContext read it server side from context.req.headers.cookie so SSR is unaffected.
Actual Result: The token and the user PII are readable by any script running on the page and there is no CSP to limit which scripts run.
Impact: Account takeover from a single XSS. The user record in the cookie also leaks name - email and mobile and is sent on every request to the domain.
Suggested Fix: Move the token to an httpOnly and secure cookie set by the backend or by a Next route handler - SSR keeps working because it reads the request header. Stop storing the whole user object in a cookie and hydrate it from the profile endpoint. Add a Content-Security-Policy header in next.config.ts.

Bug Title: handleLogout calls process.exit in its catch block which throws in the browser and would kill the server in any Node context
Bug Description: handleLogout at src/helpers/auth.ts:652-699 ends its catch with process.exit(1) at :697. In the browser process.exit is not a function so the catch itself throws a TypeError - the logout never finishes and the state left behind is inconsistent because store.dispatch(logout()) at :674 and the deleteCookie calls at :675-676 sit BEFORE the failure point only when the throw happens earlier. The catch is reachable in normal use because Router.push at :668 rejects when a route change is interrupted - for example when the user clicks another link while logout is navigating away from a my-account page. If this helper is ever evaluated in a Node context the same line terminates the process.
Preconditions: User is logged in and currently on a /my-account route so the Router.push branch at :668 executes.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in and open /my-account/orders/. 2. Trigger logout and immediately click another navigation link so the pending Router.push is interrupted and rejects. 3. Observe the catch executes process.exit.
Expected Result: Logout fails safely - the error is logged and the local session is still cleared so the user is not left in a half logged out state.
Actual Result: The catch throws a TypeError on process.exit so logout aborts. The user can remain with cookies or Redux state that disagree about whether they are signed in.
Impact: A half completed logout leaves a valid token in the cookie while the UI may show a signed out state - and the same line would terminate a Node process outright.
Suggested Fix: Remove the process.exit(1) call. Log the error and fall through to the same cleanup the success path performs so the local session is always cleared even when the logout API call or the navigation fails.

Bug Title: verifyUser converts every failure into a success false fallback so the email and phone availability check fails open and its caller error branch is unreachable
Bug Description: verifyUser at src/services/auth.ts:17-28 catches every error and returns fallbackApiRes which is success false with data undefined (src/config/constants.ts:33-37). checkEmailExists at src/helpers/auth.ts:396-436 and checkPhoneExists at :439-478 then test response.success || response.data?.exists at :412 and :455. Because the service already swallowed the rejection the try block never throws - so the catch at :420-432 that discriminates on the message User not found can never run and is dead code. A genuine network failure or a 500 from the panel is therefore indistinguishable from the user does not exist and the field is silently marked available.
Preconditions: Registration form open. The panel returns an error status when the identifier is not found which is what the dead catch at :426 was written for.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the register form. 2. Take the panel API offline or force a 500 on /verify-user. 3. Enter an email address that is already registered and leave the field.
Expected Result: The availability check fails closed or surfaces a check error to the user - the dead catch branch was written to do exactly this.
Actual Result: No error is shown. The email reads as available and registration is attempted with an address that is already taken so the failure only surfaces later from the register call.
Impact: Users are pushed into a registration attempt that cannot succeed and receive a late and confusing error. The intended error handling in the caller is unreachable code.
Suggested Fix: Let verifyUser surface the failure - either rethrow or return a discriminated result that separates request failed from user not found - then have checkEmailExists and checkPhoneExists branch on data.exists alone and show the check error state on a real failure.

Bug Title: SettingsProvider rebuilds its context value on every render so every consumer in the app re-renders
Bug Description: SettingsProvider at src/contexts/SettingsContext.tsx:69-166 builds the provider value as an inline object literal at :143-160 with no useMemo. formatPrice at :127-128 and defaultLocation at :130-139 are new references on every render as well. The provider wraps the application so every component calling useSettings at :67 re-renders whenever the provider renders - even when settings itself is unchanged. Every derived value from :76-125 is also recomputed on each render including the six getSpecificSettings scans over the settings array.
Preconditions: Any page - the provider is mounted app wide.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Render any page that has several useSettings consumers such as a product listing with prices. 2. Trigger a parent re-render. 3. Observe every consumer re-renders although settings did not change.
Expected Result: The context value is memoised on the settings identity so consumers only re-render when settings actually changes.
Actual Result: A new value object is created on every render so all consumers re-render and all derived settings are recomputed.
Impact: App wide unnecessary re-render cost on the busiest screens - product grids read currency formatting from this context for every price shown.
Suggested Fix: Wrap the derived values and the provider value in useMemo keyed on settings and wrap formatPrice in useCallback so the identity is stable across renders.

Bug Title: The response interceptor writes to the maintenance store on every successful response and notifies all subscribers each time
Bug Description: The response interceptor at src/routes/interceptor.ts:66-73 calls maintenanceStore.setMaintenance(false - null) for every 2xx response. setMaintenance at src/stores/maintenanceStore.ts:17-25 assigns a brand new state object and then calls every registered listener unconditionally - there is no check for whether the state actually changed. Subscribers therefore receive a change notification and a new state identity after every single API call even though maintenance mode was already inactive.
Preconditions: Any subscriber mounted - the layouts subscribe to render the maintenance banner.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a page that issues several API calls such as the home page. 2. Observe setMaintenance runs once per response and notifies every listener with a fresh object identity.
Expected Result: The store only notifies subscribers when the maintenance state actually changes.
Actual Result: Every successful response allocates a new state object and wakes every subscriber which re-renders the subscribing layout.
Impact: Wasted renders on every API call across the whole app - the cost scales with the number of requests a screen makes.
Suggested Fix: Return early in setMaintenance when isActive and message already equal the incoming values so listeners fire only on a real transition.

Bug Title: getCookie truncates any cookie value that contains an equals sign
Bug Description: getCookie at src/lib/cookies.ts:54-70 splits each cookie on = with const [key - value] = cookie.trim().split('=') at :61 and keeps only the first two segments. Any value containing an = is cut at the first one. Values written by setCookie survive because setCookie encodes with encodeURIComponent at :29-31 which turns = into %3D - but a cookie set by the backend is not necessarily encoded. src/services/market.ts:28-32 documents that the backend sets the market cookie itself on /markets/switch and the interceptor reads that cookie client side at src/routes/interceptor.ts:48 to build the X-Market header. Base64 or JWT style values with = padding are the common case that breaks.
Preconditions: A cookie written by the backend rather than by setCookie whose value contains an = character.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Have the backend set a cookie whose value contains = such as base64 padding. 2. Read it client side through getCookie. 3. Compare the returned value with document.cookie.
Expected Result: The full cookie value is returned regardless of any = characters inside it.
Actual Result: The value is truncated at the first = and the caller receives a corrupted value or null once JSON.parse fails.
Impact: A truncated market cookie sends a wrong or empty X-Market header so the client silently falls back to the default market - the failure mode section 7.4 of CLAUDE.md warns about.
Suggested Fix: Split on the first = only - for example by using indexOf and slice - and decode the key as well as the value.

Bug Title: serverSideAuthGuard is dead code while ten account pages each reimplement the same check inline
Bug Description: serverSideAuthGuard at src/guards/authGuard.ts:39-64 is exported and documented in CLAUDE.md 7.5 as the primary protection mechanism but no page calls it - a search across src/pages returns only the CLAUDE.md documentation reference. Instead ten my-account pages import loginRedirect directly and repeat the same getAccessTokenFromContext check plus redirect block inline - src/pages/my-account/index.tsx:12 - orders/index.tsx:23 - orders/[slug]/index.tsx:19 - addresses/index.tsx:22 - wallet/index.tsx:26 - transactions/index.tsx:20 - profile/index.tsx:58 - notifications/index.tsx:26 - wishlists/index.tsx:10 and refer-and-earn/index.tsx:14. The duplicated block is visible at orders/index.tsx:345-356.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Search src/pages for serverSideAuthGuard and observe there are no callers. 2. Compare the inline guard in any two my-account pages and observe the block is copy pasted.
Expected Result: One shared guard is called by every protected page as CLAUDE.md 7.5 prescribes.
Actual Result: The shared guard is unused and the same logic is duplicated across ten pages so a fix to the redirect behaviour has to be made ten times.
Impact: Divergence risk - a page added later can silently omit the block which is exactly what happened to checkout and payment in issue 2. Documented architecture and real code disagree.
Suggested Fix: Have each protected page call serverSideAuthGuard at the top of getServerSideProps and return its result when it is not null - then delete the inline duplicates.

Bug Title: The wildcard branch in isProtectedRoute is unreachable because no route entry uses the suffix it tests for
Bug Description: isProtectedRoute at src/guards/authGuard.ts:15-23 tests route.endsWith('/*') at :17 and strips the suffix at :18 to do a startsWith prefix match at :19. No entry in PROTECTED_ROUTES at :5-13 ends with /* so that branch never executes and every comparison falls through to the strict equality at :21. The prefix matching capability the function appears to offer does not exist in practice which is the mechanism behind issue 2.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Read PROTECTED_ROUTES at src/guards/authGuard.ts:5-13. 2. Confirm no entry ends with /*. 3. Confirm the branch at :17-19 is therefore never taken.
Expected Result: Either the route list uses the wildcard form the function supports or the dead branch is removed.
Actual Result: The branch is dead code and gives a false impression that nested routes are covered.
Impact: A reviewer or a future contributor reads the function as supporting prefix matching and adds a nested protected route expecting it to be covered when it is not.
Suggested Fix: Either add the wildcard entries the function was written for such as /my-account/* and /cart/* or drop the branch and make the prefix matching explicit.

Bug Title: The any type is used in the interceptor 503 handler and across the market service against the strict TypeScript rule
Bug Description: CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids any and requires unknown API shapes to get a type in src/types first. The 503 branch of the response interceptor casts the payload twice at src/routes/interceptor.ts:99 and :102 with (responseData as any) to read the maintenance flag and the message. src/services/market.ts declares both endpoints as ApiResponse<any> at :16 and :35 so geoDetectForCountry and switchMarket return untyped data - and the caller in src/helpers/market.ts:17 then reaches into res?.data?.suggested_market with no type safety at all.
Preconditions: None - static structure.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Read src/routes/interceptor.ts:96-103. 2. Read src/services/market.ts:14-43 and the consumer at src/helpers/market.ts:17.
Expected Result: Both the maintenance payload and the market endpoints have declared types in src/types and no any appears.
Actual Result: Four any usages remain and the market switch payload is entirely untyped on a path that decides which market the whole catalog is scoped to.
Impact: A response shape change in the market or maintenance payload passes the type checker silently and only fails at runtime - and this is the exact path that controls market scoping.
Suggested Fix: Add a MaintenanceResponse type and a GeoDetect and MarketSwitch response type in src/types and use them in place of the any casts.

Bug Title: Anonymous server side requests log a token message on every render
Bug Description: getAccessTokenFromContext at src/helpers/auth.ts:701-729 writes console.log('No valid token found in SSR context') at :723 on every server side render where no token cookie is present. That is every anonymous visit to any page whose getServerSideProps calls it. The message is noise rather than a leak - no token value is printed - but it runs on the hot SSR path and buries real errors in production logs.
Preconditions: Site running with NEXT_PUBLIC_SSR set to true and an anonymous visitor.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run the app in SSR mode. 2. Request any page whose getServerSideProps calls getAccessTokenFromContext while logged out. 3. Read the server log.
Expected Result: No log line for the ordinary anonymous case - an absent token is expected rather than exceptional.
Actual Result: One console.log per anonymous server side render.
Impact: Production log noise proportional to anonymous traffic which makes real errors harder to find. Note that compiler.removeConsole in next.config.ts strips console.log in production builds so the impact is limited to non production and to any build where that option is changed.
Suggested Fix: Drop the log line or lower it to a debug level guarded by an explicit flag.

Bug Title: Password and other credentials are sent in the URL query string instead of the request body
Bug Description: login at src/services/auth.ts:69-83 calls api.post with the /login path - a null body - and a params object at :77 so email - password and mobile are serialised into the query string rather than the body. The same pattern repeats at :32 for registerUser where password and password_confirmation are sent to /register - at :22 for verifyUser (/verify-user) and at :201 for forgotPassword (/forget-password). axios places the params object in the URL and sends a null body so the full credential set appears in the request line. Every hop that records request lines keeps them - web server access logs - reverse proxies - CDNs and APM traces. Contrast phoneLogin at :119-138 which correctly sends a body and moves only the bearer token into a header so the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
Preconditions: Any login or registration attempt. Standard web server or proxy access logging which records the request line including the query string.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the login sheet and submit any email and password. 2. Inspect the outgoing request in the devtools network tab and read the request URL. 3. Confirm the password appears as a query parameter while the request body is null.
Expected Result: Credentials travel in the POST body only and never appear in the URL.
Actual Result: email - password - mobile and password_confirmation are all query parameters on the request URL.
Impact: Plaintext passwords are written into every access log and proxy log along the request path and are readable by anyone with log access. Because users reuse passwords the exposure reaches beyond this application. Log shipping and retention widen it further.
Suggested Fix: Send these payloads as the request body rather than as params for /login - /register - /verify-user and /forget-password. Confirm the panel accepts body parameters on those routes first and coordinate the change because the API is shared with other production clients.

Bug Title: The bearer token and the full user record are persisted to localStorage by redux-persist
Bug Description: The redux-persist configuration at src/lib/redux/store.ts:12-16 lists auth in the whitelist so the entire auth slice is serialised to localStorage under the persist key root. authSlice at src/lib/redux/slices/authSlice.ts:5-15 holds access_token and the complete user object so both are written on every login through the login reducer at :26-30. This is a SECOND copy of the session and is distinct from issue 3 which covers the JavaScript readable cookie - the fix differs because this one is redux-persist configuration rather than cookie flags. localStorage also has no expiry so this copy outlives the cookie.
Preconditions: Any logged in session.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Log in. 2. Open the devtools application tab and read the localStorage key persist:root. 3. Find access_token and the user object inside the serialised auth slice.
Expected Result: The session token is not written to localStorage - persist only non sensitive auth fields such as isLoggedIn and rehydrate the session from the cookie or the profile endpoint.
Actual Result: access_token and the full user record including name - email and mobile are stored in localStorage in clear text with no expiry.
Impact: A second XSS reachable copy of the bearer token plus user PII. Because localStorage never expires the token survives a browser restart and remains replayable on a shared machine long after the cookie has gone.
Suggested Fix: Remove auth from the redux-persist whitelist or add a persist transform that strips access_token and the user PII before serialisation - then rehydrate auth state on boot from the session cookie or from /user/profile.

Bug Title: The cart slice is persisted although both CLAUDE files explicitly forbid persisting it
Bug Description: The redux-persist whitelist at src/lib/redux/store.ts:16 contains cart. Root CLAUDE.md section 7.1 lists the allowlist as auth - offlineCart - recentlyViewed and search - and src/lib/redux/CLAUDE.md states plainly that cart must not be persisted because it is a server mirror that is always re-fetched on login. cartSlice is persisted anyway so a stale server cart is rehydrated from localStorage on every boot and rendered before any revalidation completes. Separately search is absent from the whitelist which also contradicts root CLAUDE.md 7.1 - but the inline comment at :16 shows that exclusion is deliberate so only the cart entry is treated as a defect here.
Preconditions: Logged in user with items in the server cart. The cart has since changed elsewhere - another device or an admin action or a price change.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Add items to the cart and allow the state to persist. 2. Change that cart from another device or change a product price server side. 3. Reopen the storefront and read the cart before the refetch resolves.
Expected Result: The cart is not persisted - it is fetched from the server so the first paint shows either server truth or a loading state.
Actual Result: The previous cart is rehydrated from localStorage and rendered including stale quantities and stale prices until the refetch replaces it.
Impact: Customer briefly sees outdated cart contents and pricing which is most visible on a slow connection. The documented state ownership and the shipped configuration disagree which will mislead the next person to read either CLAUDE file.
Suggested Fix: Remove cart from the whitelist so the server mirror is always fetched. If persisting it is a deliberate offline decision then update both CLAUDE files to match and document what guarantees revalidation before the cart is shown.

Bug Title: Firebase auth error messages and setup toasts are hard-coded English and bypass i18n
Bug Description: getFirebaseErrorMessage at src/lib/firebase.ts:247-271 returns twelve hard-coded English strings for the Firebase auth error codes it maps at :251 :253 :255 :257 :259 :261 :263 :265 and :267 - and falls back to the raw Firebase SDK error.message at :269. Those strings reach users through addToast in src/helpers/auth.ts at :265 for apple login - :322 for sign up and :386 for resend OTP - code which uses i18n.t for every other string it renders. src/lib/firebase.ts also raises English toasts directly at :88-90 - :129-131 - :214-217 and :221-224. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any Firebase auth failure such as an expired code or the too many requests limit.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Request a phone OTP and enter an incorrect code or trigger the too many attempts limit. 3. Read the toast that appears.
Expected Result: The message renders in the active language from the locale bundles like every other auth message in the same flow.
Actual Result: The message renders in English whatever the selected language - and the default branch can surface a raw Firebase SDK string that was never written for end users.
Impact: Hindi and Arabic users meet untranslated English at the exact moment authentication fails which is a high friction point in the funnel. The default branch can also leak raw SDK wording into the UI.
Suggested Fix: Map each Firebase error code to a translation key and resolve it with t() at the call site - add the keys to en - hi and ar - and give the default branch a generic translated fallback instead of error.message. Then run npm run scan:i18n.

Bug Title: The offline cart is cleared on login even when the server rejected some items so those items are lost
Bug Description: syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:77-160 dispatches clearOfflineCart() at :110 as soon as response.success is true - before it inspects response.data.failed_items at :113. Items the server refused (out of stock - not sellable in the active market - variant gone) are therefore deleted from the only local copy the user has. The failed list is passed to a modal at :119 through the window global showFailedItemsModal - which is registered by src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 and DELETED again at :41 when that component unmounts - so if the modal is not mounted at that moment the guard at :115-118 is false and the user is told nothing at all. Either way the items are already gone from state and cannot be retried or recovered.
Preconditions: User has items in the offline cart while logged out and at least one of them is rejected by the server on sync - for example an item that went out of stock or is not sellable in the active market.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. While logged out add two products to the cart and let the offline cart persist. 2. Make one of them unsellable server side - out of stock or removed from the active market. 3. Log in and let the sync run. 4. Read the cart and the offline cart state.
Expected Result: Rejected items stay in the offline cart (or are surfaced with a retry) so the customer keeps what they chose and can act on it.
Actual Result: The whole offline cart is cleared regardless of failures. The failed items exist only inside a transient modal payload and are unrecoverable once it closes or if it never opened.
Impact: Silent loss of items the customer deliberately added. The most likely moment for this is the login that happens at the start of checkout so it directly costs conversions and the customer may not notice items are missing before paying.
Suggested Fix: Clear only the items the server accepted - keep any id present in failed_items in the offline cart - and surface the failure through normal React state rather than a window global that may not exist. Dispatch setOfflineCart with the remainder instead of clearOfflineCart.

Bug Title: clampQuantity can return a quantity below the product minimum and its second branch is unreachable
Bug Description: clampQuantity at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:55-85 first clamps into the min and max and stock window at :61-64 then snaps to the step size. The stepSize > 1 branch at :66-73 snaps to an absolute multiple of stepSize and never re-checks minQuantity - so a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2 given a desired quantity of 3 yields qty 3 at :61 - then remainder 3 % 2 = 1 at :67 - then qty = 2 at :69 - and the guard at :70 compares against stepSize rather than minQuantity so 2 is not raised back. The function returns 2 for a product whose minimum is 3. The else branch at :74-82 is dead code because it is reached only when stepSize is 1 (item.stepSize || 1 at :57 makes 0 impossible) and any value modulo 1 is 0 - so its remainder at :75 is always 0. Note the two branches also encode different models - absolute multiples in one and offsets from minQuantity in the other.
Preconditions: A product configured with a minimum quantity above 1 and a step size above 1 where the minimum is not itself a multiple of the step.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Configure a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2. 2. While logged out add it to the cart with quantity 3. 3. Read the stored offline cart quantity.
Expected Result: The quantity respects the product minimum and the step rule together - the nearest valid value at or above the minimum.
Actual Result: The quantity is snapped down to 2 which is below the configured minimum of 3.
Impact: Customer can build an offline cart that breaks the seller minimum order rule. It surfaces at login sync or at add-to-cart as a server rejection which then triggers the item loss described in issue 17.
Suggested Fix: Snap to the step relative to minQuantity and re-clamp upward afterwards so the result is never below minQuantity - and delete the unreachable else branch so a single model applies.

Bug Title: updateCartData decides the empty-cart case by string matching an English API message
Bug Description: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:15-75 tests cartRes.message == 'Your cart is empty' at :49 to choose the empty-cart branch. CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids hard-coding status strings and the panel message is free text that other clients also consume. If the wording changes or is ever localised server side the comparison silently fails and control falls into the else at :59 which dispatches setError and raises a Cart Fetch Failed toast - so a normal empty cart is reported to the customer as a system failure and the checkout state is never reset by resetCheckOutState at :51.
Preconditions: The panel returns success false with a message for the empty-cart case and that wording changes or is localised.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Empty the cart. 2. Change the panel message for the empty cart response or request it in a non English locale. 3. Reload the cart and read the UI.
Expected Result: The empty cart renders the empty state and the checkout state is reset - keyed off a stable field such as a status code or an item count rather than prose.
Actual Result: The empty cart is treated as a fetch failure - an error toast is shown and resetCheckOutState never runs so stale promo and wallet selections survive.
Impact: A routine empty cart is presented as a broken page. Because resetCheckOutState is skipped a stale promo code or wallet flag can carry into the next order.
Suggested Fix: Branch on a stable machine readable field - a status code or the item count on the payload - instead of the message text. If the panel has no such field request one and flag the contract gap rather than changing the shape unilaterally.

Bug Title: Cart status toasts are hard-coded English and one contains a typo
Bug Description: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts raises four user-facing strings with no translation - title Cart is Empty and description Add Product to processed ! at :54-55 and title Cart Fetch Failed and description Could not update cart after adding item at :63-64. The same file uses i18n.t elsewhere for the sync toasts at :126-129 so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar. The description at :55 also reads Add Product to processed ! which is not grammatical English and appears to be intended as proceed.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any empty cart or failed cart refresh.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Empty the cart or force the cart refresh to fail. 3. Read the toast.
Expected Result: The toast renders in the active language from the locale bundles.
Actual Result: The toast renders in English in every language and shows the malformed sentence Add Product to processed !.
Impact: Hindi and Arabic customers meet untranslated and grammatically broken English inside the cart which is a high intent part of the funnel.
Suggested Fix: Move all four strings into the locale bundles under a cart namespace - fix the wording to proceed - add the keys to en hi and ar and run npm run scan:i18n.

Bug Title: Merging two offline cart lines adds their quantities without applying the clamp so stock and maximum limits are bypassed
Bug Description: updateOfflineCartItem at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:179-213 handles the case where editing addons changes an item id. When the new id already exists it merges with a bare addition at :198 - state.items[nextIndex].quantity += action.payload.newItem.quantity - and then splices the old line at :199. clampQuantity is never applied to that sum even though every other write path in the slice applies it - addOfflineCartItem at :126-129 and updateOfflineCartItemQuantity at :164-167 both clamp. The merged line can therefore exceed maxQuantity and exceed stock and can also break the step rule.
Preconditions: Two offline cart lines for the same variant that differ only by addons where their combined quantity exceeds the stock or the maximum quantity.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. While logged out add a product with addon set A and again with addon set B so two lines exist. 2. Edit one line so its addons match the other and the ids collide. 3. Read the merged quantity against the product stock and maximum.
Expected Result: The merged quantity is clamped to the stock - maximum and step rules exactly as the other write paths clamp.
Actual Result: The two quantities are summed unchecked so the line can exceed the stock and the maximum quantity.
Impact: An offline cart that violates stock and quantity limits reaches the login sync and is rejected there - which then destroys the items through issue 17. The subtotal shown to the customer before login is also wrong.
Suggested Fix: Apply clampQuantity to the summed quantity at :198 exactly as addOfflineCartItem does at :126-129 - ideally by routing every quantity write through one shared helper so a future path cannot skip it.

Bug Title: Cart flows drive modals through a hidden DOM button click and a window global instead of React state
Bug Description: Two cross-component signals in the cart path bypass React entirely. updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:47 calls document.getElementById('removed-items-modal-open')?.click() to open the removed-items notice - the target is a hidden button rendered by src/components/Modals/RemovedItemsModal.tsx:62 and read back at :40. syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:115-119 calls the window global showFailedItemsModal which src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 assigns on mount and deletes at :41 on unmount - and the call is cast through (window as any) which also breaches the no any rule in CLAUDE.md section 5. Both signals fail silently when the target component is not mounted and neither is type checked.
Preconditions: The modal component is not mounted on the current route when the signal fires.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Trigger a cart refresh that returns removed_count above zero or a login sync that returns failed_items on a route where the matching modal is not mounted. 2. Observe that nothing opens and no error is raised.
Expected Result: Cross-component signals travel through React state or a store so they are type checked and cannot be lost.
Actual Result: The click target or the window function is absent so the notification is dropped without any diagnostic.
Impact: The customer is never told that items were removed from the cart or rejected during sync. It also makes the flow untestable and invisible to the type checker.
Suggested Fix: Replace both with state - a store flag or a context that the modals subscribe to - so the signal is typed and survives regardless of mount order. This also removes the two (window as any) casts.

Bug Title: A fresh idempotency key is minted on every submit so the key cannot deduplicate a retry after a timeout
Bug Description: handleCheckout at src/helpers/functionalHelpers.ts:463-568 reads state.checkout.idempotencyKey at :486 and sends it as idempotency_key at :491. Both submit paths dispatch setIdempotencyKey(genKey()) immediately before calling it - src/views/CartPageView/CheckoutSection.tsx:125 and src/components/Modals/PaymentModal.tsx:46 - so every attempt carries a different key and the server can never match two attempts. The comment at PaymentModal.tsx:43-45 shows this is deliberate: a new key lets a gateway switch create a fresh order and a double-tap is blocked by the disabled button. That reasoning holds for those two cases but not for the case idempotency keys exist for. When the request times out or the connection drops after the panel has already created the order the client sees a failure - the finally block at CheckoutSection.tsx:153-156 re-enables the button - and the next click generates a NEW key so the panel treats it as a new order.
Preconditions: User places an order and the response is lost to a timeout or a dropped connection after the panel has committed the order.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Begin checkout and place an order. 2. Interrupt the response so the client records a failure while the server has already created the order - throttle to offline after the request leaves or force a gateway timeout. 3. Press place order again on the re-enabled button. 4. Compare the resulting orders in the account.
Expected Result: The retry carries the same idempotency key so the panel recognises it and returns the original order instead of creating a second one.
Actual Result: The retry carries a newly generated key so a second order is created for the same cart - and for a prepaid method a second payment intent follows it.
Impact: Duplicate orders and potentially duplicate charges on exactly the failure mode the idempotency_key field was added to protect. The customer is billed twice and the seller ships twice.
Suggested Fix: Keep one key per checkout attempt rather than per submit - generate it when the checkout is entered or when the cart contents change and regenerate it only when the payment method actually changes so the gateway-switch case in the PaymentModal comment still works. Clear it after a confirmed success in resetCheckOutState which already runs at functionalHelpers.ts:457.

Bug Title: The wallet recharge amount is divided by 100 and multiplied by 100 again which yields a non-integer paise value for about 13 percent of amounts
Bug Description: src/components/PaymentGateway/RazorPay.tsx builds the wallet order at :136-141 by dividing the server supplied paise amount by 100 at :138 - amount: walletOrderData.payment_response.amount / 100 - and then multiplies it straight back at :145 - amount: order.amount * 100 - when constructing the Razorpay options. The round trip is pointless because payment_response.amount is already the integer paise figure the gateway wants and it is lossy in IEEE754. Measured over every paise value between 1.00 and 10000.00 the expression returns a non-integer for 131248 of 999901 values which is 13.1 percent - the smallest failing case is 0.07 which yields 7.000000000000001 and everyday values fail too including 1.10 and 2.01 and 1.15. Razorpay requires an integer amount in the smallest currency unit. The order payment path at :200-204 does NOT have this defect - it passes pr.amount through untouched - so the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
Preconditions: Wallet recharge through Razorpay for an amount whose paise value fails the round trip - roughly one value in eight.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the wallet recharge flow and choose Razorpay. 2. Enter an amount such as 1.10 or 2.01 whose paise value fails the round trip. 3. Inspect the amount passed into the Razorpay options object before checkout opens.
Expected Result: The integer paise amount from the server is passed to the gateway unchanged exactly as the order path does at :200-204.
Actual Result: A floating point value such as 110.00000000000001 is passed as the amount where the gateway requires an integer in the smallest currency unit.
Impact: Wallet recharge can fail or mismatch against the server created order for a large share of amounts. Because it depends on the specific amount it will look intermittent and be hard to reproduce from a bug report.
Suggested Fix: Delete the round trip and pass walletOrderData.payment_response.amount directly into options.amount. If a display value in major units is needed derive it separately and never feed it back into the gateway amount.

Bug Title: Wallet recharge is declared successful from the client-side gateway callback with no server confirmation
Bug Description: The wallet branch handler at src/components/PaymentGateway/RazorPay.tsx:149-157 runs onSuccess() and raises a Wallet Recharged Successfully toast as soon as the Razorpay checkout callback fires. Nothing is sent to the panel from that handler and no confirmation call is made - the callback signature at :149 is an argument-less async arrow so razorpay_payment_id and the signature that Razorpay hands to the handler are discarded rather than forwarded. The balance is only credited server side once the gateway webhook is processed so the toast asserts an outcome the storefront has not verified. The order path at :205-208 has the same shape but is materially safer because it only flips local UI state and the order status is re-read from the panel afterwards.
Preconditions: Wallet recharge completed in the Razorpay modal while the webhook is delayed - or a webhook that fails or never arrives.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Recharge the wallet through Razorpay and complete payment. 2. Read the success toast. 3. Immediately open the wallet balance before the webhook has been processed.
Expected Result: Success is confirmed against the panel - either by posting the gateway payment reference for verification or by re-reading the wallet balance before the success state is shown.
Actual Result: The success toast appears immediately on the client callback and the balance can still be unchanged behind it.
Impact: Customer is told the wallet is recharged while the balance says otherwise which drives support contacts and repeat recharge attempts. If a webhook is lost entirely the customer keeps a success message for money that was never credited.
Suggested Fix: Forward the Razorpay payment reference from the handler to a panel verification endpoint and show success only on its confirmation - or poll the wallet balance once before switching to the success state. Report the pending case honestly instead of asserting success.

Bug Title: All five payment gateway components raise hard-coded English strings to the user
Bug Description: None of the components under src/components/PaymentGateway/ route their user-facing strings through i18n. RazorPay.tsx carries the most with strings including Invalid wallet order data at :129 - Wallet Recharged Successfully! at :153 - Payment Cancelled and You have closed the Razorpay checkout. at :168-169 - Failed to start payment at :188 and the gateway descriptions Wallet Recharge at :147 and Pay Safe at :203. Paystack.tsx - BankTransfer.tsx - Stripe.tsx and FlutterwavePayment.tsx follow the same pattern. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar. The surrounding checkout code already complies - CheckoutSection.tsx uses t() for its toasts at :118 and :133 - so the payment layer is the outlier.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any payment attempt or cancellation.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Start a payment and then dismiss the gateway modal. 3. Read the toast.
Expected Result: The message renders in the active language from the locale bundles like the rest of the checkout flow.
Actual Result: Every payment gateway message renders in English whatever the language is set to.
Impact: Hindi and Arabic customers meet untranslated English at the payment step which is the highest value and least forgiving moment in the funnel. Arabic users also get left-to-right English inside an otherwise right-to-left page.
Suggested Fix: Move every user-facing string in the five gateway components into the locale bundles under a payment namespace - add the keys to en hi and ar - and run npm run scan:i18n. Cover the ondismiss and error paths as well as the success paths.

Bug Title: A failed profile fetch renders an empty editable form with no error state and saving it submits blank values
Bug Description: The profile page getServerSideProps at src/pages/my-account/profile/index.tsx:937-969 substitutes an empty object for the user on failure - initialData: response.success ? response.data : {} at :956 and initialData: {} in the catch at :965 - and passes no error flag at all. The component reads user = isSSR() ? initialData : userData at :76 and seeds the form from it at :89-96 with name: user?.name || '' and the same pattern for email - mobile - iso_2 - country and friends_code. Every field therefore renders blank with no indication that anything failed. onSubmit at :190-212 then builds new FormData(e.currentTarget) straight from those DOM fields and posts it through updateUserData so a save carries empty strings for the whole profile. Sibling pages already do this correctly - addresses uses response.success ? response.data : null at :284 and surfaces an ErrorState at :131 and the order detail page does the same at :184 - so profile is the only page in the account area that swallows the failure.
Preconditions: SSR mode with the panel returning a failure or timing out on /user/profile - a transient 500 or a dropped upstream connection is enough.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open /my-account/profile/ while the panel profile endpoint is failing or timing out. 2. Observe the form renders blank with no error message. 3. Press save without editing anything.
Expected Result: The failure is surfaced through ErrorState with a retry exactly as the addresses and order detail pages do - and the form is not rendered as an editable blank.
Actual Result: The form renders as if the account genuinely has no name - no email and no country - and saving posts those empty values back to the panel.
Impact: The customer believes their profile has been wiped and can overwrite their real name - email - country and referral code with blanks by pressing save. Whether the write lands depends on panel validation which cannot be verified from this repository - but the blank form with no error state is certain and is a violation of the four required screen states.
Suggested Fix: Return an error flag from getServerSideProps as the sibling account pages do and render ErrorState with a retry instead of the form. Do not substitute an empty object for a failed fetch - pass null so the difference between no data and failed to load is preserved.

Bug Title: Server side error messages in the account pages are hard-coded English and are rendered directly to the user
Bug Description: Four getServerSideProps handlers put untranslated English into the error prop that the page then renders as the ErrorState description - src/pages/my-account/orders/[slug]/index.tsx:167 Invalid order identifier and :195 Unable to load order details. Please try again later. - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:409 Unable to load orders. Please try again later. - and src/pages/my-account/addresses/index.tsx:284 Unable to load addresses. Please try again later. Each is passed to description={error} at the matching ErrorState - orders detail :122 and orders list :114 - so the surrounding titles come from t() while the body underneath is fixed English. Translating on the server is awkward because loadTranslations runs per request - which is likely why it was skipped - but the effect is a half translated error panel. This is the same class as issues 16 - 20 and 26 and the count across the app is now 21 files carrying literal user-facing titles.
Preconditions: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic and any server side failure on the orders or addresses pages.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Force the orders or addresses endpoint to fail so the page renders its error state. 3. Read the panel - the heading is translated and the body is English.
Expected Result: The whole error panel renders in the active language.
Actual Result: The heading renders in the selected language while the description below it stays English - and in Arabic the English body also breaks the right-to-left flow.
Impact: Customers in Hindi and Arabic get a partly translated failure message. It also blocks any future copy change because the wording lives in four page files rather than the locale bundles.
Suggested Fix: Return a stable error CODE from getServerSideProps rather than a sentence and map it to a translation key in the component - which keeps the server handler free of translation concerns and puts the wording in en hi and ar. Then run npm run scan:i18n.

Bug Title: The retry action on four account error states triggers a full page reload rather than refetching
Bug Description: Four account pages wire their ErrorState retry to a hard browser reload - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:116 - src/pages/my-account/transactions/index.tsx:69 - src/pages/my-account/wallet/index.tsx:107 and src/pages/my-account/refer-and-earn/index.tsx:120 all pass onRetry={() => window.location.reload()}. Every one of these pages already holds an SWR binding that exposes mutate - the orders page destructures the SWR result at :207-208 and the addresses page at :63 - so a scoped refetch is available and is not used. A reload discards the entire SWR cache for the session - re-runs getServerSideProps - re-downloads the bundle - loses scroll position and resets any filter or page held in component state.
Preconditions: Any account page that has rendered its error state.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the orders page with the panel failing so the error state renders. 2. Press retry. 3. Observe a full navigation rather than an in-place refetch - the whole app re-initialises and the list returns to its first page.
Expected Result: Retry refetches only the failed request through the SWR mutate the page already has and leaves the rest of the app state intact.
Actual Result: The browser performs a full reload which throws away all cached data and any filter or pagination the user had set.
Impact: Slow and heavy recovery from a transient error - the customer loses their place in a filtered order list and pays a full page load for what is one request. On a poor connection this is the worst possible moment to re-download everything.
Suggested Fix: Pass the SWR mutate the page already destructures as the onRetry handler so only the failed request is retried. Keep the reload only for the offline and maintenance screens where a full re-initialisation is actually the point.

Bug Title: decimal_separator is the only market format field with no fallback so a null value prints the literal text null inside every price
Bug Description: formatCurrency at src/helpers/currency.ts merges the market rules over its defaults with const f = { ...DEFAULT_FORMAT - ...(format || {}) } and then reads each field. Every other field is defensive - thousand_separator falls back through separator || '' inside groupThousands - negative_format through (f.negative_format || '-{n}') - decimal_places through a typeof number guard - and symbol_position degrades safely because anything that is not the string after is treated as before. decimal_separator alone is interpolated raw into `${grouped}${f.decimal_separator}${decPart}` with no guard. A spread copies a key that is present with a null or undefined value and overwrites the default so a market whose format block carries decimal_separator: null produces the string 1234null50. Executed against the real function: a null yields $1234null50 and an explicit undefined yields $1234undefined50 while an omitted key correctly yields $1234.50. The MarketFormat interface at src/types/market.ts:2-10 declares every field optional so an absent value is expected by design.
Preconditions: A market whose format block returns decimal_separator as null or as an explicitly present undefined rather than omitting the key. The panel controls this value per market.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Configure or mock a market format where decimal_separator is null. 2. Render any price through formatPrice from SettingsContext. 3. Read the output.
Expected Result: The default separator is used whenever the market does not supply one - the same way every other field in the same function already degrades.
Actual Result: The literal text null is printed between the whole and decimal parts of every price on the site.
Impact: Every price - cart total - wallet balance and order amount in that market renders as unreadable text. It is a single misconfigured field away and affects the entire storefront at once rather than one screen.
Suggested Fix: Guard the field like its siblings - use (f.decimal_separator || '.') at the interpolation - or filter null and undefined values out of the format object before the spread so a present-but-empty field cannot beat the default.

Bug Title: An unparseable or missing amount is rendered as a genuine zero so a wallet balance that failed to load shows as no money
Bug Description: formatCurrency at src/helpers/currency.ts coerces its input with const num = Number(amount) and then falls back with const safe = Number.isFinite(num) ? num : 0. Any value that is not a finite number - undefined - null - an empty string or a string that is already grouped such as 1234.50 with a separator - becomes 0 and is formatted as a real amount. Executed against the real function: an already grouped string returns $0.00 and a null returns $0.00. The reachable case is src/components/Cart/WalletCard.tsx:60 which renders wallet?.formatted_balance ?? formatPrice(userData?.wallet_balance) - so when the wallet payload is missing or the balance field is absent the customer is shown a formatted zero balance rather than a loading or error state. The server-formatted branch is correct - this is only about the client fallback.
Preconditions: Wallet payload missing or its balance field absent - for example the wallet endpoint failing while userData is present from a cached session.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Load the wallet screen with the wallet endpoint failing so wallet is undefined and userData.wallet_balance is absent. 2. Read the available balance figure.
Expected Result: A missing amount is distinguishable from a real zero - render a placeholder or the loading state rather than a formatted number.
Actual Result: The balance renders as a fully formatted zero which is indistinguishable from an account that genuinely holds no money.
Impact: A customer with money in their wallet is told the balance is zero when the fetch failed. That drives support contacts and can cause them to abandon a wallet-funded checkout. The same silent zero applies anywhere formatPrice receives a missing value.
Suggested Fix: Return null or a placeholder from formatCurrency when the input is not finite and let the caller decide what to render - or keep the zero only for a genuine numeric zero and have WalletCard show its loading state while the wallet payload is absent.

Bug Title: The recharge amount field strips the decimal point so a decimal entry is silently multiplied by one hundred
Bug Description: handleAmountChange at src/components/Modals/DepositModal.tsx:39-47 sanitises the field with inputValue.replace(/\\D/g - '') which removes every non-digit character including the decimal separator - then parses the remaining digits with parseInt at :42 and writes the result back into the controlled input at :47. Typing 100.50 therefore leaves the digit run 10050 and the field becomes 10050 - one hundred times the intended amount. The separator is not rejected and no validation message is raised - the digits either side of it are simply joined. If whole-currency recharge is the intent then the correct behaviour is to reject or truncate the fractional part rather than concatenate it into the whole part.
Preconditions: Any user typing or pasting a decimal amount into the wallet recharge field.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open the wallet recharge modal. 2. Type 100.50 into the amount field. 3. Read the value the field now holds.
Expected Result: Either the decimal is accepted as a fractional amount or the separator is rejected with a message - the digits after it are never promoted into the whole-currency part.
Actual Result: The field silently becomes 10050 which is one hundred times the amount that was typed.
Impact: A customer intending to add 100.50 is presented with a payment for 10050 in the market currency. The value is visible in the field so it can be caught - but the transformation is silent and the payment sheet that follows shows only the inflated figure.
Suggested Fix: Sanitise to a single decimal-aware numeric pattern rather than stripping all non-digits - or if the recharge is deliberately whole-currency then truncate at the separator and surface a message explaining that fractional amounts are not accepted.

Bug Title: The maximum recharge amount is a hard-coded number that ignores the market currency
Bug Description: The deposit submit handler at src/components/Modals/DepositModal.tsx:84 rejects any amount above the literal 1000000 with the message from deposit.error.exceed. The limit is not read from settings and is not scaled by the active market currency - so the same numeric ceiling applies whether the market prices in a strong currency or one where a routine purchase already runs to six or seven figures. CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids hard-coding business values of this kind and section 7.4 requires monetary behaviour to follow the active market rather than a fixed constant. There is no matching minimum either - the only lower bound is the parsedAmount <= 0 check at :73 - so a recharge of the smallest possible unit is accepted while the ceiling is arbitrary.
Preconditions: A market whose currency has a low unit value so that 1000000 units is an ordinary rather than an exceptional amount.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Switch to a market whose currency runs to large nominal figures. 2. Attempt a wallet recharge of an ordinary local amount above 1000000 units. 3. Observe the amount is rejected as exceeding the maximum.
Expected Result: The recharge ceiling comes from settings and is expressed per market so it means the same thing in every currency.
Actual Result: A single hard-coded ceiling applies to every market so it is far too low in some and far too permissive in others.
Impact: Customers in high-nominal-value currencies cannot recharge ordinary amounts while customers in other markets face no meaningful ceiling at all. The limit also cannot be changed without a code release.
Suggested Fix: Read the minimum and maximum recharge from the wallet or payment settings that SettingsContext already exposes and fall back to a documented default only when the setting is absent. Flag the need for the setting to the panel if it does not exist yet rather than adding another constant.

Bug Title: A failed catalog fetch is converted into an empty list so every product listing reports no results instead of an error
Bug Description: The SWR fetcher inside useInfiniteData at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:65-79 returns res.data only when res.success is true - otherwise it logs to the console at :77 and returns an empty array at :78. Returning a value rather than throwing means SWR records a SUCCESS so the error field the hook exposes at :166 is never populated. The effect layer at :86-99 then reads swrResponse?.data || [] and swrResponse?.total || 0 - and because the fallback value is a bare array those both resolve to empty and zero. Downstream the search page destructures the hook at :150-156 and does not take error at all so it has nothing to render even if the hook had set it. Every listing built on this hook therefore renders its empty state on a backend failure. CLAUDE.md section 6.3 requires a distinct error state and explicitly forbids rendering a failed request as an empty result.
Preconditions: Any catalog endpoint returning success false or failing - a 500 from the panel or a market with no permission to the requested scope.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Force /products to fail or return success false. 2. Open the search results page or any listing built on useInfiniteData. 3. Read what the page shows.
Expected Result: The listing shows the error state with a retry - distinct from a genuine no-results outcome.
Actual Result: The listing shows the empty state so the customer is told their search matched nothing when the request actually failed.
Impact: Customers are told a category or search has no products whenever the backend fails - which hides outages - suppresses retries and looks like missing inventory. Because the hook backs every catalog listing the behaviour is repo wide rather than one screen.
Suggested Fix: Throw from the fetcher when res.success is false so SWR populates error - then surface that error through the hook and render ErrorState with refetch at each consumer. Keep the empty state strictly for a successful response with zero items.

Bug Title: Catalog SWR cache keys do not include the active market so a cached list survives a market switch
Bug Description: useInfiniteData builds its cache key at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:53-55 from the dataKey and a JSON serialisation of extraParams only. The market is never part of it - it travels as the X-Market header applied by the interceptor - so two different markets produce the SAME key for the same listing and the second market reads the first market payload straight from cache. No SWR key anywhere in src includes a market value which was confirmed across all 29 files that call useSWR. The search page shows the pattern at :158 where dataKey is /productsSearch: plus the query - specific about the query and blind to the market. This is the mechanism underneath issue 1 but it is a DIFFERENT root cause and needs a different fix - issue 1 is that resolveMarketForCountry only revalidates the settings key while this is that the keys are not market scoped in the first place. Fixing either one alone leaves the other as a latent trap.
Preconditions: Two markets with differing catalogue or pricing and a user who switches market after browsing.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Browse a category or run a search in market A. 2. Switch to market B. 3. Return to the same listing without a hard reload and read the cached results.
Expected Result: The cache key carries the market so a switch produces a different key and the listing refetches under the new X-Market header.
Actual Result: The key is identical across markets so the previous market cached payload is served.
Impact: Wrong market inventory and pricing shown after a switch. Making the key market aware fixes the whole class at once rather than requiring every future switch site to remember to invalidate.
Suggested Fix: Include the active market code in the SWR key for every market-scoped fetch - either by adding it to extraParams in useInfiniteData or by prefixing dataKey with the market. That way a switch changes the key and no explicit invalidation is needed.

Bug Title: The documented per-volatility stale times are not implemented for any catalog fetch
Bug Description: CLAUDE.md section 7.3 sets a stale time per data type - product lists about 2 minutes - product detail and reviews about 5 minutes - categories brands stores and settings about 30 minutes - and instructs that dedupingInterval and revalidateOnFocus must be set per volatility rather than accepting defaults. Across the 29 files that call useSWR only 3 set dedupingInterval and all three are account screens - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx - wishlists/index.tsx and notifications/index.tsx. No catalog fetch sets it - useInfiniteData passes only revalidateOnFocus and revalidateOnMount at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:80-83 - so every catalog list - product detail - category - brand and store request falls back to the SWR default deduping window of 2 seconds instead of the documented minutes. The focus half of the rule is largely done - 25 of the 29 files do set revalidateOnFocus - so this is specifically about the stale windows.
Preconditions: Normal browsing where the same catalog data is requested by more than one component or revisited within the documented stale window.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a listing and navigate away and back within a minute. 2. Watch the network panel. 3. Observe the catalog request is re-issued rather than served from cache for the documented window.
Expected Result: Catalog requests are deduplicated for the window the documentation specifies per data type.
Actual Result: Requests are deduplicated for only 2 seconds so browsing re-fetches near-static data such as categories and brands repeatedly.
Impact: Avoidable request volume against the panel on the busiest screens and slower navigation for the customer - most wastefully on categories brands and stores which the documentation treats as changing about every 30 minutes.
Suggested Fix: Set dedupingInterval per the section 7.3 table at each catalog call site or centrally in useInfiniteData with a per-data-type override - and keep the revalidateOnFocus values already in place.

Bug Title: Debug logging scaffolding was left in the product page server render path
Bug Description: The product detail getServerSideProps at src/pages/products/[slug]/index.tsx:288-345 contains five console.log calls added for debugging - a decorative banner reading ========== SSR PRODUCT PAGE ========== at :300 - the requested slug at :301 - a product existence flag at :309 - the product slug at :313 and a call labelled Fetched Product Full at :318 which passes JSON.stringify(data?.initialProduct?.slug - null - 2) so despite the label it prints only the slug and formats a plain string with indentation. This runs on every server render of the most requested page on the storefront. compiler.removeConsole in next.config.ts strips console.log from production builds so the runtime cost is limited to development and to any build where that option changes - but the block is debugging scaffolding rather than intended logging and the misleading label invites a future reader to trust it.
Preconditions: Any server side render of a product detail page.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run the app in SSR mode outside a production build. 2. Request any product page. 3. Read the server log.
Expected Result: No debug scaffolding on the hot path - any retained logging is deliberate and accurately labelled.
Actual Result: Five debug lines including a decorative banner are written per product page render and one is labelled as the full product while printing only the slug.
Impact: Log noise on the highest traffic server path in development and a misleading label that will mislead the next person debugging this page. Related to issue 12 which covers the same class on the SSR auth path.
Suggested Fix: Delete the five console.log calls. If any server side visibility is wanted here keep one accurately labelled line behind an explicit debug flag rather than an unconditional block.

Bug Title: API supplied HTML including seller authored product and store descriptions is rendered without any sanitisation
Bug Description: The storefront renders API HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML in seven places and applies no sanitisation at any of them. HTMLRenderer at src/components/Functional/HTMLRenderer.tsx:10-16 passes its html prop straight through and is used for the product additional-detail block at src/components/Products/ProductDetailPage/AdditionalDetailSection.tsx:96 and for four CMS pages - about-us/index.tsx:67 - privacy-policy/index.tsx:67 - shipping-policy/index.tsx:47 and terms-and-conditions/index.tsx:72. Two further call sites inline the same pattern - src/components/Cards/PromoCard.tsx:83 renders promo.description and src/components/StoreProfile.tsx:154 renders store.description. No sanitisation library exists in the project at all - package.json has no DOMPurify or sanitize-html and a repo wide search for sanitize finds only the numeric input strippers in DepositModal and WithdrawModal. HyperCommerce is a MULTI SELLER marketplace per CLAUDE.md section 1 so product and store descriptions originate from sellers rather than from trusted staff. The storefront therefore depends entirely on the panel stripping active content on write - a dependency that is neither documented nor verifiable from this repository.
Preconditions: A seller or content author able to store HTML in a product description - a store description or a promo description - and panel side sanitisation that is absent or incomplete.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Store markup containing an active payload such as an onerror attribute in a product description through whatever authoring path the panel provides. 2. Open the product detail page as a customer. 3. Observe whether the markup executes in the page origin.
Expected Result: API supplied HTML is sanitised on render with an allow-list so stored markup cannot introduce script execution regardless of what reaches the database.
Actual Result: The HTML is injected verbatim into the page so the storefront provides no defence of its own and the outcome depends entirely on panel behaviour.
Impact: If panel sanitisation is missing or bypassable this is stored XSS on the most visited pages of the storefront. It compounds directly with issue 3 - no Content-Security-Policy and a JavaScript readable bearer token - and issue 14 - the same token in localStorage - so a single successful injection yields session theft rather than mere defacement.
Suggested Fix: Sanitise on render with an allow-list inside HTMLRenderer and apply the same helper at the two inline call sites so there is one choke point. Treat this as defence in depth rather than a replacement for panel sanitisation - and confirm with the panel team what it strips on write so the two layers are documented rather than assumed.

Bug Title: The 22 redesign sandbox routes and the design system page are publicly crawlable and indexable
Bug Description: src/pages/redesign holds 22 route files and src/pages/design-system.tsx is a further one. None of the 23 emits a robots meta tag of its own - a search across src/pages/redesign and design-system.tsx for SEOHead - DynamicSEO - PageHead or next/head returns nothing - and public/robots.txt contains no Disallow entry for either path so both fall under the blanket Allow: / at the top of the file. Absence of a robots meta means indexable by default. Where a redesign page does inherit the default layout it is worse than neutral because SEOHead at src/SEO/SEOHead.tsx:53 emits a hard-coded index - follow with no prop to override it. These pages render the sandbox mock data from src/redesign/data/mock.ts rather than live catalogue data.
Preconditions: Production deployment with the redesign routes present - which is the current state since the sandbox ships in the same build as the storefront.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Deploy the storefront. 2. Request /redesign/home/ or /design-system/ as a crawler with no referrer. 3. Check for a robots meta in the response and check public/robots.txt for a matching Disallow.
Expected Result: Internal design sandbox routes are excluded from indexing - by a noindex meta or a robots.txt Disallow or by not shipping them in a production build at all.
Actual Result: All 23 routes are served with no robots restriction and are eligible for indexing alongside the real storefront pages.
Impact: Search engines can index 23 internal pages carrying mock product data and placeholder copy. They compete with the real category and product pages for the same terms - they expose unreleased design work publicly - and any that duplicate a live screen create genuine duplicate content against the page they were built to replace.
Suggested Fix: Add Disallow entries for /redesign/ and /design-system/ to the robots.txt template that scripts/update-robots.mjs consumes and emit a noindex meta on those routes. The stronger fix is to exclude the sandbox from production builds entirely so the routes do not exist outside development.

Bug Title: The generated sitemap advertises two routes that do not exist including one the project has formally deprecated
Bug Description: The static route list in scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs:13-27 is hand maintained and has drifted from the real route tree. Two entries have no matching page. /delivery-zones/ at :18 is submitted with priority 0.6 although there is no src/pages/delivery-zones directory - and CLAUDE.md section 9.11 states the feature is deprecated product wide and must not be ported or flagged as a gap - so the sitemap is actively advertising a removed feature. /products/ at :20 is submitted with priority 0.9 although src/pages/products contains only the [slug] detail route and the search route with no index page - so the listing URL the sitemap treats as the highest priority catalogue entry point does not resolve. Verified by checking every static entry against the filesystem: the other eleven all have a matching page.
Preconditions: Any production build - the sitemap is regenerated during npm run build and submitted through the Sitemap directive in robots.txt.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run npm run build to regenerate public/sitemap.xml. 2. Read the entries for /delivery-zones/ and /products/. 3. Request both URLs and observe they do not resolve to a real page.
Expected Result: Every URL in the sitemap resolves to a real page - a sitemap is a statement that these URLs are canonical and worth crawling.
Actual Result: Two of the thirteen static entries point at routes that do not exist - one of them at the highest priority given to any catalogue URL.
Impact: Crawl budget is spent on URLs that cannot resolve and repeated 404s from a submitted sitemap degrade the trust search engines place in the whole file. Advertising the deprecated delivery-zones path also contradicts an explicit project rule.
Suggested Fix: Remove both entries from the static list. Better - derive the static routes from the actual pages directory during generation so the list cannot drift again - and add a build time assertion that every sitemap URL resolves to a page.

Bug Title: Six features write to localStorage directly and logout clears only two of the keys so prior user data survives sign out
Bug Description: CLAUDE.md section 5 states plainly that localStorage must not be written directly because redux-persist owns it. Six modules bypass that with fourteen write sites - src/hooks/useRecentSearches.ts:39 stores the search history under recentSearches - src/services/adTrackingService.ts:41 and :45 store ad tracking state - src/pages/shopping-list/index.tsx:103 :109 :115 and :121 store the shopping list keywords - src/components/Modals/DeepLinkModal.tsx:113 :128 :182 and :199 store four app-install flags - src/components/Functional/CookieConsent.tsx:28 and :33 store the consent choice - and src/components/Functional/FirebaseInitializer.tsx:107 stores the FCM token. Because none of this is in the persist store the logout path has to clean up by hand and it does so incompletely - handleLogout at src/helpers/auth.ts:658-659 removes only shoppingListActiveKeywordString and shoppingListKeywords. Everything else survives sign out including the previous account search history and ad tracking state and the FCM token that identifies the device to the push service.
Preconditions: Shared or public device where one account signs out and another signs in - a library machine or a shared family browser or a demo device.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Sign in and use the site so recent searches and ad tracking entries accumulate. 2. Sign out through the account menu. 3. Read localStorage and open the search bar as the next user.
Expected Result: Signing out clears everything tied to the previous session - which is what routing this state through redux-persist would give automatically since its store is purged on logout.
Actual Result: Only the two shopping list keys are removed. The previous account search history remains visible in the search bar to the next user and the ad tracking state and FCM token remain on the device.
Impact: The next person to use the device sees what the previous account searched for which is a direct privacy leak on shared machines. The stale FCM token can also keep the device associated with the signed-out account for push delivery.
Suggested Fix: Move this state into redux-persist slices so the existing purge on logout covers it - that is what the documented rule is for. Where a value genuinely must outlive the session such as the cookie consent choice keep it in localStorage deliberately and document the exception - then extend handleLogout to clear every remaining session-scoped key rather than the two it knows about.

Bug Title: The share landing route re-implements the product page server logic and has drifted from it so a removed product returns a soft 404
Bug Description: src/pages/share/products/[slug].tsx re-exports the product page component at :45 but supplies its own getServerSideProps at :9-43 rather than reusing the canonical one. The two have diverged. The product page checks the fetch result and returns notFound: true when no product came back - src/pages/products/[slug]/index.tsx:324-335 - while the share route returns props unconditionally at :27-33 with no such check. A share link to a deleted or invalid product therefore answers 200 with an empty product page rather than 404. The props type permits it because initialProduct is declared optional at :33 of the product page so nothing fails loudly. The share route also omits country_iso2 which the canonical route reads with getCountryIso2FromContext and passes into the same fetch at :294 and :306 so the delivery estimate that depends on it is absent for every visitor arriving through a share link. Line 43 also carries an undefined as any cast which is the issue 11 class.
Preconditions: A share link pointing at a product that has since been deleted or unpublished or a share link with a malformed slug.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Share a product link so it points at /share/products/{slug}/. 2. Delete or unpublish that product. 3. Open the share link and inspect the HTTP status and the rendered page.
Expected Result: The route behaves exactly like the canonical product page - 404 for a missing product and the same delivery estimate for a present one.
Actual Result: The response is 200 with an empty product page and no delivery estimate is shown even when the product exists.
Impact: Soft 404s from share links get indexed and accumulate as thin duplicate pages - and share traffic which is by nature first-time visitor traffic sees a degraded product page missing the delivery information the canonical page shows. Duplicated server logic will keep drifting every time the canonical route changes.
Suggested Fix: Export the product page getServerSideProps and reuse it from the share route rather than maintaining a second copy - or at minimum add the notFound guard and pass country_iso2 so the two match today. Reusing it also removes the undefined as any cast.
